title: The context window
teaser: How much the AI can keep in mind

basics.say: When you chat, the AI doesn't remember the way you do. Each time, it rereads the part of the conversation it can see.
That visible part is called the context window: your messages, its replies and any files you shared.
The window has a size limit, measured in tokens. In a very long chat, the oldest messages can slide out of view.
Out of view means forgotten. That's why an assistant can lose track of something you said earlier in a long chat.
Tip: for a new task, start a fresh chat, or recap the key points. You keep the AI focused on what matters.

deeper.say: Modern models have big windows – often hundreds of thousands of tokens, enough for a long report or even several books.
Bigger isn't always better: details buried in the middle of a very long context can get less attention.
Some apps offer 'memory'. Behind the scenes, they save notes and slip them back into the context window for you.
The golden rule: whatever the AI needs for this task should be inside the window – clear, and close to your request.

takeaway: The AI only knows what fits in its context window right now.
